back: All production costs, fixed and variable, are charged to units; inventory is valued at full production cost.
Opening inventory + production cost - closing inventory (all at full production cost per unit), adjusted for under- or over-absorbed overhead.
Selling, distribution and administration costs are period costs, deducted in full in the period; never included in inventory.
Fixed overhead is carried forward in closing inventory, so profit is higher than if all fixed overhead were charged to the year.
Fixed overhead brought forward in opening inventory is released into cost of sales, so profit is lower.
Opening units + units produced - units sold.
Selling price = full cost + mark-up (a percentage of cost).
Arbitrary overhead bases; unit cost depends on budgeted output; hides cost behaviour; may mislead short-run decisions.
Inventory valuation for financial statements, full-cost pricing and quotations, recovering all production costs.
